name: Muzhappilangad Drive-in Beach
tagline: Asia’s longest drive‑in beach — icon of Malabar coastal road trips
summary: A long, hard-packed sandy shore where vehicles may drive for several kilometres. Famous for sunsets, birdlife and Dharmadam Island; popular on coastal road trips.
description: Muzhappilangad Drive‑in Beach is a long, hard-packed sandy shore on the Malabar coast near Thalassery in Kannur district. The beach runs parallel to NH‑66 and offers one of the rare legal drive‑on stretches in Asia, used by cars and motorbikes during low tide.

It matters because the unique combination of compact sand, coastal scenery and easy road access makes it a classic stop on Kerala coastal road trips. Visitors get wide open beach driving, views of Dharmadam Island at low tide, good sunset photo opportunities and local Malabar food shacks near the shore.

The area is also important for birdwatching — rocky outcrops and shallow waters attract migratory and resident shorebirds during the cooler months — and it is part of a state-backed development project that aims to upgrade walkways and visitor facilities.

Practical visitors find Muzhappilangad rewarding as a short stop (7–8 km from Thalassery) or a half‑day excursion from Kannur; driving the sand is best at low tide and with caution where construction rubble or rocks are present.
highlights: Drive along a 3–4 km stretch of packed sand (legal drive‑in area).
Walk to or view Dharmadam Island at low tide.
Reliable Malabar sunsets and shorebird watching in winter.
Local shacks serving Malabar cuisine near the beach.
Easy stop on NH‑66 between Thalassery and Kannur.

sections.heading: Background
body: Muzhappilangad is known locally as the state’s (and region’s) signature drive‑in beach: the compact, gently sloping sand allows vehicles to run safely along kilometres of shore when conditions are right. The beach lies parallel to NH‑66 between Thalassery and Kannur and is a long-standing tourist draw for Malabar coastal travel.

The Kerala government has included Muzhappilangad — together with nearby Dharmadam Beach and Dharmadam Island — in a comprehensive development plan funded by KIIFB; early phases added walkways, playgrounds and basic visitor infrastructure as part of a wider upgrade.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Drive the beach: experience the unusual thrill of a seaside drive (keep speed low and obey local instructions). Driveable distance is commonly reported as around 3.4–4 km along the compact sand; choose low tide for the safest and most complete route.
Dharmadam Island and birdlife: at low tide you can walk close to Dharmadam Island; the rocky fringes and shallow waters are good for shorebird and migrant sightings in winter months.

Sunset, photography and food: the beach is a favourite for sunset photography. Small local shacks and stalls near the shore offer Malabar snacks and seafood — a convenient complement to a short coastal stop.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Best time is post‑monsoon and winter (roughly October–February) when the sea calms, skies clear and migratory birds arrive. Low tide gives the best driving and walking access to Dharmadam Island.

Safety and rules: check local notices before driving on the sand — local regulations and conditions change with tides and construction. Recent reporting notes scattered construction stones in parts of the beach; avoid driving in concealed/rocky areas and confirm current safety status with the Panchayat or local authorities before you drive.

Getting there: reach the beach easily by road from Thalassery (about 7–8 km) or Kannur (roughly 13–16 km); regular buses and taxis serve the route. Nearest major railheads are Thalassery and Kannur; Kannur International Airport (Mattanur) is the closest airport (see official travel pages for exact distances and current services).

latest.text: News reporting highlights jagged granite stones and leftover rubble on a stretch of the beach that pose hazards to vehicles and pedestrians; locals and panchayat members urge authorities to clear the debris and finish cleanup work.
Muzhappilangad Grama Panchayat posts a notice announcing a cleaning drive for the Drive‑In Beach and community cleanup activities (page notes a planned cleaning on '19th September').

visitorInfo.bestTime: October–February (post‑monsoon/winter; low tide best for driving and visiting Dharmadam Island)
visitorInfo.howToReach: By road from Thalassery (about 7–8 km) or Kannur (around 13–16 km); buses and taxis stop near the beach. Nearest railheads: Thalassery and Kannur. Nearest airport: Kannur International Airport (Mattanur); check current services before travel.
etiquette: Drive only at low tide, keep speed low, and obey local guidance — sand looks firm but tide can hide soft or rocky patches.
Check recent local notices or ask the Panchayat before driving — recent reports warn of construction stones and rubble in places.
Bring footwear for walking among rocks and shells, and avoid disturbing shorebirds or any nesting marine life.
Confirm facilities, water‑sports availability and any parking or vehicle rules with local authorities before you travel.
